title: dome-mirror overwrite-propagation: git->FUSE replication of overwrite-mode latest-*-summary.txt surfaces (DIRECTIVE-20260612-001) -- sibling to PROP-091
problem: build.js syncToWorkspace (invoked by dome-mirror via sync-workspace-step4c.js) propagates git->FUSE with create-only / category-skip semantics, so overwrite-mode files that already exist on a session's FUSE mount go permanently stale at whichever version that session last wrote. Two sub-cases, both observed across the 12 latest-*-summary.txt rescue surfaces: (a) 'workspace'-classified summaries (latest-decider/baby/score/rewrite-summary.txt) are skipped wholesale by syncToWorkspace's category==='workspace' branch; (b) append_only / append_only_glob summaries are either filtered out (the walker copies '.json' only, so .txt under monitor/changes, monitor/integrity is never copied) or copied ONCE then frozen by walkAppendOnly's create-only 'if (fs.existsSync(dst)) continue' (monitor/tinker/latest-tinker-summary.txt). Operator symptom 2026-06-12: tinker's June 11/12 report-*.json files propagated cleanly (create-mode), but latest-tinker-summary.txt stayed at the June 10 18:38 version the cowork session last wrote locally; operator misread morning state as 'tinker hasn't run since June 10' and only caught it by manually fetching origin. This is the structural sibling of PROP-091's delete-propagation gap -- same root (create-only git->FUSE copy in syncToWorkspace), opposite operation (overwrite vs delete).

investigation_answers.q1_content_hash_vs_mtime: Chosen: content-hash for difference detection PLUS git-commit-time-vs-durable-sentinel for direction. Rationale: with a small explicit allow-list (12 files) a sha256 per file per cycle is negligible, and content-hash is the only way to avoid needless writes (and the mtime churn they would cause). Raw FUSE-mtime is deliberately NOT used for direction -- PROP-082 established that FUSE mtimes are not comparable across sessions (each mount stamps its own). Instead the pass reuses the same durable signal sync-workspace-step4c.js already computes for needSync: the last successful sync sentinel timestamp (lastSentinelAt). A file is propagated only when (content differs) AND (its last git-commit time > lastSentinelAt), i.e. git genuinely received a newer write since our last sync. A FUSE copy that differs only because THIS session wrote a fresher-but-unpushed version has an OLDER last-git-commit time, so it is classified 'fuse-ahead-skip' and left for workspace-sync to rescue up first.
investigation_answers.q2_allowlist_explicit_vs_derived: Explicit enumeration (operator's stated lean; constraint forbids implicit 'sync anything in monitor/' clauses). The OVERWRITE_ALLOWLIST hard-codes all 12 latest-*-summary.txt surfaces with a per-line note on why each is currently un-propagated. Deriving from CLAUDE.md OWNERSHIP's workspace filter was rejected: (a) it would miss the append_only_glob frozen case (latest-tinker-summary.txt is NOT 'workspace'-classified -- it lives in monitor/tinker/ append_only_glob), so an OWNERSHIP-derived list would omit the directive's own headline example; (b) implicit derivation is exactly the unbounded-blast-radius shape PROP-051 warns against. Maintenance cost (add a line when a new agent summary appears) is accepted; a missed entry degrades to the status quo (that one summary stays stale), never to over-writing.
investigation_answers.q3_canonicalness_reframe: These files are written per-session but are cross-session CANONICAL = latest-in-git. There is one logical decider, one logical tinker, etc.; the scheduler runs each in whatever session it picks, and workspace-sync already rescues the most-recent writer's version up to origin/main. dome-mirror's job is to replicate that authoritative version DOWN into other sessions' FUSE. OWNERSHIP classification is UNCHANGED -- the 'workspace' files stay 'workspace' (so workspace-sync keeps rescuing them FUSE->git) and the append_only_glob files stay append_only_glob (so per-run report-*.json immutability is untouched). The pass is additive and orthogonal to OWNERSHIP: it operates on the FUSE tree directly via fs, after build.js sync-workspace has run, so it does not require and does not change any category. The direction guard guarantees a session's own fresh write is never the thing being clobbered -- only versions where git is provably newer are pushed down.
investigation_answers.q4_unified_vs_sibling: Sibling PROP (this PROP-092), NOT folded into PROP-091. Rationale, ranked by ship-safety (the directive's tie-breaker): (1) PROP-091 is mid-rollout -- Phase 0 landed 2026-06-11, Phase 1 manifest observation (>=3 days) is in progress; adding a second behavior to its config and code would reset/muddy its acceptance gates. (2) The two passes have different risk profiles: delete (PROP-091) is blocked by FUSE's missing unlink() and may be permanently manifest-only; overwrite (this PROP) uses in-place copyFileSync truncate-write, which already works on FUSE every publish, so it can reach Phase 2 on its own faster timeline. (3) Independent pause/rollback: each pass has its own config key, so disabling one never touches the other. The directive's explicit 'Do NOT change PROP-091's logic; this is purely additive' is honored -- PROP-091's deletePropagationPass and its config key are untouched; PROP-092 adds a parallel function and a parallel config key in the same helper.

proposed_fix.summary: Add an overwritePropagationPass(fuseRoot, lastSentinelAt) function to sync-workspace-step4c.js, invoked in the SAME place PROP-091's delete pass runs -- the needSync branch, immediately after a successful 'node build.js sync-workspace', only when syncExit===0. Results merge into the existing single run sentinel under a new 'overwrite_propagation' key (preserves PROP-066's exactly-one-sentinel invariant). Config-gated, ships enabled=false (manifest-only). Two-guard candidate rule: allow-listed path AND (git HEAD content != FUSE content) AND (git last-commit time > lastSentinelAt). Safety per PROP-051: explicit bounded allow-list, abort gate, EPERM->manifest-only fallback, runs only after confirmed upstream movement (non-FF already aborted upstream). No OWNERSHIP change, no build.js change, no PROP-091 change, dome-mirror stays a FULL clone.

files_to_modify.change_1_define_function: Insert the overwritePropagationPass() definition (full code in new_code below) immediately AFTER the existing deletePropagationPass() definition (i.e. just before the 'State holders' comment block).
files_to_modify.change_2_invoke: In the final needSync write branch, right after the existing delResult block, add a parallel: let ovwResult = { ran:false, mode:null, aborted:'sync-failed' }; if (syncExit === 0) { const fuseRootMatch2 = syncOut.match(/Sync to workspace \(([^)]+)\)/); const fuseRoot2 = fuseRootMatch2 ? fuseRootMatch2[1] : null; ovwResult = fuseRoot2 ? overwritePropagationPass(fuseRoot2, lastSentinelAt) : { ran:false, mode:null, aborted:'no-fuse-workspace-resolved-from-build-output' }; }  (fuseRoot is already parsed for the delete pass; reuse that variable if convenient.)
files_to_modify.change_3_sentinel: Add overwrite_propagation: ovwResult to the final writeSentinel(sync-workspace-runs-...) payload object (alongside the existing delete_propagation: delResult).
files_to_modify.explanation: Single-file change, mirrors PROP-091's integration shape exactly. Reuses the helper's existing sh()/CONFIG_PATH/ROOT plumbing and lastSentinelAt (already computed in Step 2). Merges into the existing sentinel; no second sentinel written. copyFileSync truncate-write is the same primitive build.js copyIfExists uses for git-owned files, so overwriting an existing FUSE file is a proven-working operation (unlike unlink).

files_to_modify.find: (append key to existing JSON object, sibling to delete_propagation)
files_to_modify.explanation: Operator-curated gate. enabled=false is the shipped Phase-0 state (manifest-only). File is already classified 'git' in build.js OWNERSHIP -- no ownership-table change needed. per_cycle_cap/abort_abs default 20 (> the 12-entry allow-list, so they are defensive sanity bounds, not throttles).

safety_gates.explicit_allowlist: Blast radius is bounded by a 12-entry hard-coded list -- no directory globs, no derivation. The pass cannot touch any file outside the list even if guards mis-fire.
safety_gates.content_hash_gate: A file is only written when git HEAD content differs from FUSE content (sha256). Identical files are skipped, so the pass never churns mtimes and never triggers a spurious workspace-sync push.
safety_gates.direction_guard: Propagation only when git's last-commit time for the path > lastSentinelAt. This is the load-bearing protection against clobbering a session's own fresher-but-unpushed write: such a write has an older last-git-commit time and is classified 'fuse-ahead-skip'. Uses durable git commit time + sentinel baseline, never raw FUSE mtime (PROP-082).
safety_gates.runs_only_after_successful_sync: Invoked only in the needSync branch when syncExit===0. true-non-ff origin is classified and aborted by the existing Step 4/6 logic BEFORE this branch (helper exits 1), so the pass never runs against rewritten history.
safety_gates.abort_gate: If would-write count exceeds abort_abs (default 20, i.e. larger than the whole allow-list) the pass aborts with zero writes and records the reason in the sentinel. Defensive -- should be unreachable given the allow-list size.
safety_gates.eperm_fallback: copyFileSync truncate-write works on FUSE in the normal case (build.js does it every publish), but on any EPERM/EACCES/ENOTSUP the pass records 'copy-unsupported-on-fuse' and degrades to manifest-only, exactly like PROP-091's unlink fallback.
safety_gates.loop_safety: After a copy, FUSE byte-matches git HEAD, so workspace-sync's smart_copy cmp -s content-equality short-circuit (workspace-sync.md ~line 481) returns 0 without pushing. PROP-045 anti-reversion is a second backstop. No git<->FUSE ping-pong.
safety_gates.full_clone: dome-mirror stays a FULL clone (PROP-051/PROP-084). A sparse/partial clone would make the clone's working-tree copies (the git HEAD side of the hash compare) absent, which the content-hash gate treats as 'not in git HEAD -> skip' -- so a partial clone degrades to no-op, never to over-write. The dome-mirror working-tree-size>=100 check is the primary defense and is unchanged.

test_plan: T1 frozen-append-glob positive (the directive case): scratch clone at HEAD + fake-FUSE dir holding an OLDER monitor/tinker/latest-tinker-summary.txt (older content, and set lastSentinelAt earlier than git's commit for the file). Run with enabled=false -> sentinel lists 1 candidate decision='git-newer-overwrite', written=0. Flip enabled=true -> FUSE file now byte-matches git, written=1.

T2 fuse-ahead negative (the data-loss-protection case, MUST pass before rollout): fake-FUSE holds a NEWER local-only content for latest-decider-summary.txt, and git's last commit for that path is OLDER than lastSentinelAt. Run -> decision='fuse-ahead-skip', candidates=0, written=0. The local write is preserved for workspace-sync.
T3 in-sync negative: FUSE content byte-equals git HEAD -> file not listed as candidate (content-hash short-circuit).

T4 fuse-absent create: allow-listed file exists in git HEAD, absent on FUSE -> decision='fuse-absent-create', written=1 when enabled (covers the never-copied .txt-in-append_only and unclassified-dir sub-cases).

T5 workspace-owned coverage: confirm latest-decider/baby/score/rewrite-summary.txt are reached by the pass even though build.js sync-workspace logged 'skip (workspace-owned)' for them -- proves the pass is orthogonal to OWNERSHIP.
T6 non-ff edge: force-reset upstream, run helper -> exits 1 with non-ff-abort sentinel; grep confirms overwrite pass never logged (it lives after the abort, in the needSync branch).

T7 EPERM probe (real FUSE, Phase 1): run enabled=true against the real workspace once -> expect real writes (copyFileSync works on FUSE) OR aborted='copy-unsupported-on-fuse' with files intact. Record which world we are in.
T8 loop-safety: after a Phase-2 write, run workspace-sync (or simulate its smart_copy on the same path) -> cmp -s equal -> no push, no commit.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (land, inert): merge the function + config key with enabled=false. Every dome-mirror cycle now writes overwrite_propagation.{candidates,items} into its sentinel. Zero FUSE writes.

Phase 1 (observe, >=3 days): operator reviews manifests. Acceptance: zero 'fuse-ahead-skip' rows that should actually have propagated (direction guard not over-blocking) AND zero 'git-newer-overwrite' rows pointing at a file the operator knows the local session legitimately owns this cycle. Run T7 EPERM probe once.

Phase 2 (enable): operator flips enabled=true via clone-and-push (config is git-owned). Because overwrite uses copyFileSync (no unlink), Phase 2 is expected to actually write, unlike PROP-091 where manifest-only-forever is a live possibility.

Phase 3 (verify): tinker Mode 3 checks 7 days post-enable that the 12 allow-listed FUSE summaries track git HEAD content (a fresh dome-mirror cycle reports 0 candidates in steady state once all sessions converge) and that no abort/EPERM sentinels fired.
Pause/rollback: flip enabled=false (single config push); the pass is stateless so disable is instant and complete, and independent of PROP-091's toggle.
tradeoffs: Gain: the operator's FUSE view of every agent's latest-run summary stops going stale across sessions; the specific 2026-06-12 misdiagnosis class ('agent hasn't run since X' when it actually ran in another session) is closed. Cost/counterargument (surfaced deliberately): these summaries are operator-UX convenience surfaces, NOT pipeline-correctness inputs -- agents read canonical state from fresh git clones, not from FUSE summaries, so nothing in the automated pipeline is currently BROKEN by the staleness; the operator could alternatively git pull or read GitHub raw. The case for fixing anyway: it cost real operator time and a wrong morning read, the fix is cheap, bounded, and reversible (git is canonical, so a bad overwrite self-heals next cycle), and 'the operator can trust the FUSE view' has compounding value across every future morning. Residual risk (bounded): if two sessions write the SAME summary within one sync window, last-writer-in-git wins and a transiently-newer local copy may be overwritten before its own workspace-sync push -- but for per-run GLOBAL summaries last-writer-in-git IS the intended semantics, and convergence is a single cycle. Inherent risk: any automated git->FUSE write is the disaster-class power 2026-05-21 says to gate -- mitigated by the 12-entry allow-list, dual content+direction guards, Phase-0 inert ship, and the fact that overwrite (unlike delete) is recoverable from git.
estimated_impact: Operator-facing trust restoration for 12 summary surfaces; eliminates a recurring 'stale FUSE summary' false-signal that has already caused one documented misdiagnosis. Negligible compute (12 sha256 + up to 12 small file copies per needSync cycle). No disk reclamation (this is a correctness/UX fix, not a space fix like PROP-091).
why_human_needed: Two decisions mirror PROP-091: (1) approve the allow-list membership and the thresholds (per_cycle_cap=20 / abort_abs=20); (2) approve granting dome-mirror automated FUSE-WRITE capability for these paths. Overwrite is lower-risk than PROP-091's delete (recoverable from git, no unlink dependency), but it is still the 2026-05-21 disaster-class power and deserves the deliberate gate. Manifest-only-then-enable after >=3 days of clean manifests is the recommended conservative path.
